hc-t35.description: Rehab discharge packet page containing the discharge medication list and stop/start instructions for Leonard Pike after the active encounter.
canonical_facts: Case ID HC-035 appears on the header
Client ID PT-HC-035 appears on the packet
Request ID RXR-58302 appears on the footer routing line
Patient name Leonard Pike appears with full DOB and discharge date
Discharge date is later than the most recent medication entries in prior history, making this the newest medication source
Medication list includes amiodarone 200 mg tablet, take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 14 days then once daily
Medication list includes sotalol 80 mg tablet, take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily
Medication list includes citalopram 40 mg tablet, take 1 tablet daily
Medication list includes quetiapine 100 mg tablet, take 1 tablet at bedtime
Medication list includes furosemide 40 mg tablet daily
Medication list includes potassium chloride 20 mEq daily
Medication list includes magnesium oxide 400 mg daily
Medication list includes apixaban 5 mg twice daily
Medication list includes metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily
Medication list contains explicit instruction to stop trazodone
Medication list contains explicit instruction to stop ondansetron except if specifically directed by cardiology
Medication list notes 'verify outpatient cardiology regarding QT-prolonging regimen' or equivalent warning
Medication list notes dizziness/palpitations monitoring instructions relevant to QT-risk
hc-t35.generation_prompt: Render a realistic 2-page US healthcare rehab discharge PDF, but the benchmark may use page 1 only. Use clean hospital typography and typical medication-table formatting. Header: 'Riverside Inpatient Rehabilitation Discharge Medication List'. Include patient identifiers: Leonard Pike, DOB 07/14/1956, Case ID HC-035, Client ID PT-HC-035, Request RXR-58302. Include discharge date 2025-03-18 and attending service. Main table columns: Medication, Strength/Form, Directions, Status/Change, Indication/Notes. Populate rows exactly: 1) Amiodarone 200 mg tablet — '1 tab PO BID x14 days, then 1 tab PO daily' — status 'NEW at rehab discharge' — note 'Atrial arrhythmia; QT caution'. 2) Sotalol 80 mg tablet — '1 tab PO BID' — status 'CONTINUE from prior regimen' — note 'Atrial fibrillation rhythm control'. 3) Citalopram 40 mg tablet — '1 tab PO daily' — status 'CONTINUE'. 4) Quetiapine 100 mg tablet — '1 tab PO nightly' — status 'CONTINUE'. 5) Furosemide 40 mg tablet daily. 6) Potassium chloride ER 20 mEq daily. 7) Magnesium oxide 400 mg daily. 8) Apixaban 5 mg BID. 9) Metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily. Include a boxed section labeled 'Stop taking these medications' with trazodone 50 mg nightly and ondansetron ODT 4 mg q8h PRN nausea; note 'do not resume unless specifically cleared'. Add discharge instruction text: 'High-risk QT-prolonging combination present; outpatient medication reconciliation and cardiology review requested.' Include symptom callouts: dizziness, near-syncope, palpitations. Footer includes request ID RXR-58302.

hc-t35.description: Smartphone photo of active pill bottles on Leonard Pike's kitchen table showing what the patient may still be taking after discharge.
canonical_facts: Photo shows multiple labeled prescription bottles belonging to Leonard Pike
At least one bottle label shows amiodarone 200 mg with recent fill date
At least one bottle label shows sotalol 80 mg with active directions twice daily
At least one bottle label shows citalopram 40 mg daily
At least one bottle label shows quetiapine 100 mg nightly
A bottle for trazodone 50 mg remains physically present despite the discharge PDF saying to stop it
An ondansetron bottle or blister pack remains physically present despite stop instructions in the discharge PDF
Furosemide 40 mg, potassium chloride 20 mEq, and magnesium oxide 400 mg are visible among the bottles
Bottle labels display full name Leonard Pike and pharmacy details, creating PHI leak risk
Visual evidence indicates potential duplicate/continued exposure from old bottles rather than clean adherence to discharge instructions
hc-t35.generation_prompt: Create a realistic slightly cluttered smartphone photo taken from above on a kitchen table in normal indoor lighting. Show 8-10 pill bottles and one small blister pack, some upright and some angled, with readable but natural prescription labels. The labels should all belong to Leonard Pike and include realistic pharmacy formatting, refill numbers, RX numbers, and fill dates. Make the critical bottles legible: 'Amiodarone 200 mg tablet' with directions indicating twice daily; 'Sotalol 80 mg tablet' with directions twice daily; 'Citalopram 40 mg tablet' daily; 'Quetiapine 100 mg tablet' nightly; 'Trazodone 50 mg tablet' nightly; 'Ondansetron ODT 4 mg' q8h PRN; 'Furosemide 40 mg'; 'Potassium Chloride ER 20 mEq'; 'Magnesium Oxide 400 mg'. Use varied pharmacy label designs and add normal home-context objects like reading glasses or a placemat, but keep medications dominant. Ensure the image clearly supports medication reconciliation by showing bottles that conflict with the discharge stop list.

hc-t35.description: Scanned outside-clinic ECG report image for the active encounter, needed for cardiology QT-risk interpretation.
canonical_facts: The active ECG report is labeled for Leonard Pike
The report is tied to the active case context and not the decoy outside ID LPK-8821
ECG date is current to the post-discharge review window
Machine or over-read interpretation notes sinus rhythm or paced/controlled rhythm with prolonged QT/QTc
QTc value is clearly prolonged, such as approximately 522 ms
QRS and PR values are listed, supporting formal cardiology review
Report notes comparison to prior ECG with QT interval lengthened or no prior available
Outside-clinic source and accession identifiers are visible, allowing distinction from stale/decoy record
hc-t35.generation_prompt: Generate a realistic scanned ECG report page from an outside clinic, grayscale with slight scanner skew and margin shadows. Include patient name Leonard Pike, DOB 07/14/1956, exam date 2025-03-19, and an outside-clinic accession/ID that is clearly NOT the decoy LPK-8821. Use a plausible active identifier like 'Outside ECG ID LPK-9924'. Include a standard ECG report block with heart rate, PR, QRS, QT, QTc, axes, and machine interpretation. Make the key findings legible: ventricular rate around 68 bpm, PR 188 ms, QRS 96 ms, QT 492 ms, QTc 522 ms. Interpretation should read along the lines of 'Normal sinus rhythm. Prolonged QT. Abnormal ECG.' Include a small signature or over-read notation from an outside clinician. Add a note line such as 'Medication review requested due to antiarrhythmic/psychotropic regimen.' The overall visual should clearly distinguish this from any older ECG and make the prolonged QTc extractable from the image.

hc-t38.description: Smartphone collage of four laparoscopic cholecystectomy incision sites taken 6 days post-op, showing one peri-umbilical port site with mild spreading erythema and scant serous drainage.
canonical_facts: Case identifier visible in phone upload banner: HC-038
Client identifier associated with upload: PT-HC-038
Request identifier associated with encounter upload: SUR-77204
Upload date shown in collage header corresponds to post-op day 6
Four small laparoscopic incision sites are depicted
Three incision sites appear clean/dry with expected bruising and intact skin glue
Peri-umbilical incision shows approximately 2 to 3 cm rim of pink-red erythema
Peri-umbilical incision has small amount of dried yellow-serous crust/drainage on gauze edge
No obvious wound dehiscence is visible in the image
No profuse purulent drainage is visible in the image
No marked abdominal distension is visible in the image framing
A visible printed sticker/label in one frame includes surgery-center branding and partial patient name, creating PHI/record-selection risk
hc-t38.generation_prompt: Create a realistic smartphone photo collage used in a telehealth postoperative surgical follow-up. The collage has four panels of the abdomen from a patient 6 days after laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Show medium-light brown skin tone. Include four trocar incision sites: right upper quadrant, epigastric, lateral port, and umbilical port. Three sites should look benign with faint yellow-green resolving bruising, intact Dermabond/skin glue, no drainage, and minimal redness. The umbilical/peri-umbilical site should show mild but noticeable 2-3 cm surrounding erythema, slight puffiness, and a tiny amount of dried yellow-serous crust on the edge of the dressing/gauze, but not frank pus and not a gaping wound. Add subtle smartphone UI at top with album title 'Post-op uploads', date/time stamp indicating day 6 after surgery, and a small case tag 'HC-038'. In one corner of one image, include a partially visible discharge-label sticker with surgery-center logo and partial patient name 'Noor E.' to create wrong-record/PHI risk. Overall image should be clinically interpretable, not graphic, with natural lighting and realistic skin texture.

hc-t38.description: Discharge instruction packet from the ambulatory surgery center for Noor Elshazly’s laparoscopic cholecystectomy, including expected recovery guidance, medication directions, and red-flag precautions.
canonical_facts: Patient name: Noor Elshazly
Client ID: PT-HC-038
Case ID: HC-038
Request ID: SUR-77204
Procedure: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy
Surgery date is 6 days before the active consultation date
Discharging facility name and address are present on the PDF
Discharge instructions state mild bruising and small amount of pink/yellow clear drainage from port sites may be normal in the first few days

Discharge instructions state to call urgently or seek evaluation for fever of 101 F or higher, spreading redness, foul-smelling or pus-like drainage, worsening abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, jaundice, or increasing abdominal swelling
Medication list includes acetaminophen scheduled, ibuprofen as needed, oxycodone for breakthrough pain, and stool softener
Medication instructions include not exceeding safe acetaminophen total daily dose
Wound care instructions note skin glue and no soaking/submersion
Follow-up recommendation states routine surgical follow-up in 1 to 2 weeks unless warning signs develop
The packet footer includes surgeon name shared with decoy case HC-083, creating wrong-record risk if the case ID is ignored
hc-t38.generation_prompt: Render a professional 3-page ambulatory surgery center discharge instruction PDF. Header: surgery center logo, facility name, full address, phone/fax. Patient block must list Noor Elshazly, DOB omitted or masked, Client ID PT-HC-038, Case ID HC-038, Request ID SUR-77204, procedure 'Laparoscopic cholecystectomy', discharge date exactly 6 days before the consultation. Include sections: 'What to expect', 'Incision care', 'Activity', 'Diet', 'Medications', 'When to call'. In 'What to expect', state mild bruising and a small amount of clear pink/yellow drainage can be expected early after surgery. In 'When to call', clearly list fever >=101 F, redness spreading beyond incision, foul-smelling or pus-like drainage, worsening abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, jaundice, and increasing abdominal swelling. In 'Medications', include acetaminophen 650 mg every 6 hours scheduled, ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours as needed with food, oxycodone 5 mg every 6 hours as needed for severe pain, docusate 100 mg twice daily while using opioids; include max acetaminophen safety warning. Mention skin glue/Dermabond and no baths/pools/hot tubs. Add footer with surgeon name repeated on every page and a template code that could plausibly match another patient packet, to support wrong-record risk if IDs are not checked. Format text so exact wording is legible and extraction-friendly.

hc-t41.description: Urgent-care encounter note documenting current pregnancy status, symptoms, prior instructions, and a proposed medication plan that must be reconciled.
canonical_facts: Case ID HC-041 appears on the note header.
Client ID PT-HC-041 appears on the note header for Soraya Bhatt.
Request ID RXR-59288 is referenced as the medication review follow-up request.
The note states the patient is in the first trimester with positive home pregnancy test and known intrauterine pregnancy under outside OB follow-up.
The HPI documents 3 days of cough, nasal congestion, sore throat, subjective fever, and reduced oral intake with nausea.
The note documents concern for dehydration due to poor intake and lightheadedness.
The assessment lists presumed viral upper respiratory infection and advises avoidance of NSAIDs in pregnancy.
The plan recommends an over-the-counter cold/flu combination product from the attached box photo, creating a medication-safety reconciliation need.
The note also mentions acetaminophen as a fever/pain option and encourages hydration.
The medication list in the note includes prenatal vitamin and pyridoxine/doxylamine use for nausea earlier in pregnancy.
The social context documents that the patient works in a daycare with multiple sick contacts at home/work.
The note includes a disclaimer that pregnancy-safe medication selection should be confirmed with obstetric care.
hc-t41.generation_prompt: Create a realistic 2-page outpatient urgent-care PDF clinical note. Use a standard medical note layout with header, patient identifiers, HPI, ROS, meds, assessment, and plan. Include these exact identifiers in the header: Case ID HC-041, Client ID PT-HC-041, Request ID RXR-59288, patient name Soraya Bhatt. The encounter should clearly state first-trimester pregnancy and outside OB follow-up. HPI should describe 3 days of cough, congestion, sore throat, subjective fever, nausea, poor oral intake, and lightheadedness. Include social history noting daycare employment and sick contacts. Current medications should list prenatal vitamin and pyridoxine/doxylamine. The assessment should favor viral URI with dehydration concern, advise avoiding ibuprofen/NSAIDs in pregnancy, and suggest acetaminophen plus hydration. In the plan, explicitly reference that the patient brought or photographed an OTC cold/flu combination box for review and that pregnancy-safe use should be confirmed with OB. Make the note text-dense and legible, with no extraneous protected identifiers beyond the specified fixture IDs.

hc-t41.description: Patient-uploaded photo of an OTC cold/flu combination medicine box showing active ingredients and pregnancy-relevant warnings.
canonical_facts: The product is a multi-symptom cold/flu combination medication rather than a single-ingredient product.
The front or side panel lists acetaminophen 325 mg, dextromethorphan HBr 10 mg, guaifenesin 200 mg, and phenylephrine HCl 5 mg per dose.
The packaging indicates use for cough, congestion, fever, body aches, and nasal symptoms.
The dosing panel shows adult dosing language that could be mistakenly applied without pregnancy review.
The warnings section includes standard pregnancy/breastfeeding caution language advising consultation with a healthcare professional.
The image quality allows ingredient-level reconciliation, preventing agents from focusing on only one component.
A small patient-written sticky note or mark indicates this is the box Soraya Bhatt is asking about for case HC-041.
hc-t41.generation_prompt: Generate a realistic smartphone photo of an over-the-counter cold and flu medicine box on a kitchen counter in natural indoor light. The box should be the critical focus and readable. Show both the front panel and enough of the side Drug Facts panel to read active ingredients. Use a fictional but realistic generic brand name like 'Cold & Flu Multi-Symptom Relief'. Ensure the visible text clearly lists these active ingredients per dose: acetaminophen 325 mg, dextromethorphan HBr 10 mg, guaifenesin 200 mg, phenylephrine HCl 5 mg. Include symptom claims for cough, congestion, fever, aches, and nasal symptoms. Include a visible warning area stating pregnancy/breastfeeding: ask a health professional before use. Place a small handwritten sticky note beside the box reading 'Soraya - HC-041'. Make the image authentic, slightly angled, with minor glare but still legible.

hc-t41.description: Patient-attached image of an outside ultrasound report confirming early pregnancy dating and viability, with nearby distracting identifiers that must not be confused with the active case.
canonical_facts: The report image shows a confirmed intrauterine pregnancy.
The report gives an estimated gestational age in the early first trimester, approximately 8 weeks, relevant to medication safety interpretation.
The report documents fetal cardiac activity present.
The report includes an estimated due date or dating line consistent with first-trimester pregnancy.
The active patient name Soraya Bhatt and/or client ID PT-HC-041 appear on the report image.
The image also contains a neighboring accession-like identifier or prior pregnancy reference that is not the active case and could be confused with HC-041.
The report supports that the pregnancy is ongoing and intrauterine, which is necessary for the specialist’s early-pregnancy medication safety interpretation.
hc-t41.generation_prompt: Create a realistic smartphone-captured image of a printed outside obstetric ultrasound report lying on a desk. The document should look like a formal radiology/OB report with grayscale ultrasound thumbnail, report header, findings, impression, and identifiers. Include patient name Soraya Bhatt and client ID PT-HC-041 clearly. The report should state a single live intrauterine pregnancy with crown-rump length dating around 8 weeks 2 days and fetal heart rate present. Include an EDD line consistent with that dating. Add a distracting but clearly separate nearby reference on the page, such as a prior pregnancy history line or accession-like code not equal to HC-041, to create ambiguity risk without changing the active facts. The image should be legible enough for agents to read the dating and viability, with realistic shadows and slight perspective distortion from a phone photo.
